title: حِكَايَةُ الصُّغْرَى: مَدِينَةُ الْحِجَارَةِ السُّودِ وَالشَّابُّ النَّاجِي
titleEn: The Youngest Sister's Tale: The City of Black Stone and the Surviving Youth
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 121–127 (Night 17, continuing directly from nights-16), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 17 gives the tale of the housekeeper-lady of the Baghdad house, the youngest of three sisters, told to the caliph to explain why her two elder sisters are the beaten black dogs. Three sisters inherit a thousand dinars each; the two elder marry, are ruined and abandoned by their husbands, return in rags and are twice taken in and restored by the youngest, until they sail together with her merchant ship, which loses its course into an unknown sea. They reach a city whose whole population — king, queen, guards, beasts — has been turned to black stone, and in its palace find one young man alive, reciting the Qur'an in a hidden chapel. His own story (a Zoroastrian court, a secret Muslim nurse, three heavenly warnings ignored for three years, the wrath that turned the city to stone) is interrupted by a poem in praise of his beauty and by Shahrazad's dawn. Both poems are printed pointed in the edition and are copied as printed. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةَ عَشَرَ قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿata ʿashara qālat
sentences.l: So when it was the seventeenth night, she said:

sentences.t: بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهَا لَمَّا تَقَدَّمَتْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahā lammā taqaddamat bayna yaday amīri al-muʾminīna qālat
sentences.l: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when she had come forward between the two hands of the commander of the believers, she said:
sentences.i: It has reached me, O fortunate King, that when she came and stood before the Commander of the Faithful, she said:

sentences.t: لِي حَدِيثٌ عَجِيبٌ وَهُوَ أَنَّ هَاتَيْنِ الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ السُّودِ أَخَوَاتِي وَنَحْنُ كُنَّا ثَلَٰثَ أَخَوَاتٍ شَقَائِقَ مِنْ أُمٍّ وَأَبٍ
sentences.tr: lī ḥadīthun ʿajībun wa-huwa anna hātayni al-kalbatayni al-sūdi akhawātī wa-naḥnu kunnā thalātha akhawātin shaqāʾiqa min ummin wa-abin
sentences.l: To me is a wondrous tale, and it is that these two bitches, the black-ones, are my sisters; and we were three sisters, full-sisters, from a mother and a father,
sentences.i: I have a wondrous tale to tell: these two black bitches are my sisters. We were three sisters, born of one mother and one father,
sentences.n: السُّودِ is a plural adjective standing beside a dual noun (الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ), where Classical Arabic would use a dual; a common Middle Arabic looseness, kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَأَنَّ هَاتَيْنِ الْبِنْتَيْنِ الْوَاحِدَةَ الَّتِي عَلَيْهَا أَثَرُ الضَّرْبِ وَالْأُخْرَى الْخُوشْكَاشَةَ مِنْ أُمٍّ أُخْرَى
sentences.tr: wa-anna hātayni al-bintayni al-wāḥidata allatī ʿalayhā athuru al-ḍarbi wa-al-ukhrā al-khūshkāshata min ummin ukhrā
sentences.l: and that these two girls, the one upon whom is the mark of the beating, and the other, the khūshkāsha, are from another mother.
sentences.i: and that these two other girls, the one who bears the marks of the beating and the other, the khūshkāsha, were born of a different mother.
sentences.n: الْخُوشْكَاشَةَ is an unfamiliar word, apparently foreign (perhaps Persian). From the context, 'from another mother', it seems to mean a half-sister or something close to it; the sense is uncertain, so it is left untranslated in the literal layer.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَاتَ وَالِدُنَا أَخَذَ كُلٌّ حِصَّتَهُ مِنَ الْمِيرَاثِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā māta wālidunā akhadha kullun ḥiṣṣatahu mina al-mīrāthi
sentences.l: So when our father died, each took his share from the inheritance.
sentences.i: When our father died, each of us took her share of the inheritance.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَيَّامٍ تُوُفِّيَتْ وَالَّتِي خَلَّفَتْ لَنَا ثَلَٰثَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda ayyāmin tuwuffiyat wa-allatī khallafat lanā thalāthata ālāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: And after days she was taken-in-death, and the-one-who left to us three-of thousands of dinars.
sentences.i: A few days later she died, leaving us three thousand dinars.
sentences.n: The subject of تُوُفِّيَتْ ('she died') is not named. The context (a parent leaving an inheritance) points to the mother, and وَالَّتِي ('and she who') may stand for a word meaning 'our mother'; it is read here as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ كُلُّ بِنْتٍ مِيرَاثَهَا أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat kullu bintin mīrāthahā alfa dīnārin
sentences.l: So each girl took her inheritance, a thousand dinars.

sentences.t: وَكُنْتُ أَنَا أَصْغَرَهُمْ سِنًّا
sentences.tr: wa-kuntu anā aṣgharahum sinnan
sentences.l: And I was, I, the smallest of them in years.
sentences.i: I was the youngest of them.

sentences.t: فَتَجَهَّزُوا أَخَوَاتِي وَتَزَوَّجَتْ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ بِرَجُلٍ وَقَعَدُوا مُدَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-tajahhazū akhawātī wa-tazawwajat kullu wāḥidatin bi-rajulin wa-qaʿadū muddatan
sentences.l: So they made-themselves-ready, my sisters, and each one married with a man, and they sat a period.
sentences.i: My sisters made ready, and each married a man, and they settled down for a time.
sentences.n: The verbs فَتَجَهَّزُوا and قَعَدُوا are masculine plural although the subject is women, and تَزَوَّجَتْ takes بِـ where Classical takes a direct object; all are Middle Arabic features kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ عَمِلَ مَتْجَرًا وَأَخَذَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ زَوْجَتِهِ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَ رَمَوْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma inna kulla wāḥidin ʿamila matjaran wa-akhadha kullu wāḥidin min zawjatihi alfa dīnārin wa-ramawnī
sentences.l: Then indeed each one made a trading-venture, and each one took from his wife a thousand dinars, and they threw me.
sentences.i: Then each husband set up in trade and took a thousand dinars from his wife, and they cast me off.
sentences.n: رَمَوْنِي is printed 'they threw me', though the sense wants 'they threw them (the wives) off'; it is kept as printed. The conjunction وَ stands apart from it in the edition, at the end of a line.

sentences.t: فَغَابُوا خَمْسَ سِنِينَ وَضَيَّعَ أَزْوَاجُهُمُ الْمَالَ وَانْكَسَرُوا وَتَرَكُوهُمْ فِي بِلَادِ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-ghābū khamsa sinīna wa-ḍayyaʿa azwājuhumu al-māla wa-inkasarū wa-tarakūhum fī bilādi al-nāsi
sentences.l: So they were absent five years, and their husbands wasted the money, and were broken, and left them in the lands of the people.
sentences.i: They stayed away five years; their husbands squandered the money and were ruined, and left their wives stranded in foreign lands.
sentences.n: بِلَادِ النَّاسِ, literally 'the lands of the people', is the idiom for foreign countries, where one is a stranger. وَانْكَسَرُوا ('they were broken') means they went bankrupt.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ خَمْسِ سِنِينَ جَاءَتْنِي الْكَبِيرَةُ فِي صِفَةِ شَحَّاذَةٍ وَعَلَيْهَا ثِيَابٌ مُشَرْمَطَةٌ وَإِزَارٌ وَسِخٌ قَدِيمٌ وَهِيَ فِي أَنْجَسِ الْأَحْوَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda khamsi sinīna jāʾatnī al-kabīratu fī ṣifati shaḥḥādhatin wa-ʿalayhā thiyābun musharmaṭatun wa-izārun wasikhun qadīmun wa-hiya fī anjasi al-aḥwāli
sentences.l: So after five years the elder one came to me in the guise of a beggar-woman, and upon her were tattered clothes and a dirty, old wrap, and she was in the filthiest of conditions.
sentences.i: After five years my eldest sister came to me in the guise of a beggar, wearing tattered clothes and a dirty old wrap, in the foulest of states.
sentences.n: مُشَرْمَطَةٌ ('tattered, in shreds') is a colloquial-looking word; the feminine singular adjective agrees with the plural noun ثِيَابٌ as is usual for non-human plurals.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا ذَهَلْتُ عَنْهَا وَلَمْ أَعْرِفْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dhahaltu ʿanhā wa-lam aʿrifhā
sentences.l: So when I was bewildered away from her, and did not know her.
sentences.i: I was so bewildered at the sight of her that I did not know her.
sentences.n: The وَ before وَلَمْ introduces the main clause after فَلَمَّا ('when ... then'), so the sentence reads as one thought.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي لَمَّا عَرَفْتُهَا قُلْتُ لَهَا مَا هَٰذَا الْحَالُ
sentences.tr: thumma innī lammā ʿaraftuhā qultu lahā mā hādhā al-ḥālu
sentences.l: Then indeed I, when I knew her, said to her: 'What is this state?'
sentences.i: Then, when I recognised her, I said to her, 'What is this plight?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا أُخْتَنَا مَا بَقِيَ الْكَلَامُ يُفِيدُ وَجَرَى الْقَلَمُ بِمَا حَكَمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā ukhtanā mā baqiya al-kalāmu yufīdu wa-jarā al-qalamu bi-mā ḥakama
sentences.l: So she said: 'O our sister, speech no longer remains profiting, and the pen has run with what it ruled.'
sentences.i: She said, 'Sister, talk no longer avails; the pen has run according to what it decreed.'
sentences.n: 'The pen has run' is a set phrase for destiny: what fate has written has been carried out. أُخْتَنَا is 'our sister', though she is addressing one person.

sentences.t: فَأَرْسَلْتُهَا إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ وَأَلْبَسْنَاهَا بَدْلَةً
sentences.tr: fa-arsaltuhā ilā al-ḥammāmi wa-albasnāhā badlatan
sentences.l: So I sent her to the bath, and we clothed her in a suit.
sentences.i: I sent her to the bath, and we dressed her in a fresh suit of clothes.
sentences.n: The narrator slips from 'I' (أَرْسَلْتُهَا) to 'we' (أَلْبَسْنَاهَا), presumably including her household; kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَا أُخْتِي أَنْتِ عِوَضُ أَبِي وَأُمِّي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahā yā ukhtī anti ʿiwaḍu abī wa-ummī
sentences.l: And I said to her: 'O my sister, you are the replacement of my father and my mother,
sentences.i: I said to her, 'My sister, you stand to me in place of my father and mother.

sentences.t: وَالْإِرْثُ الَّذِي نَابَنِي مَعَكُمْ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ الْبَرَكَةَ وَأَنَا أُزَكِّي عَلَيْهِ وَأَحْوَالِي جَلِيلَةٌ وَأَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ سَوَاءٌ
sentences.tr: wa-al-irthu alladhī nābanī maʿakum qad jaʿala Allāhu fīhi al-baraka wa-anā uzakkī ʿalayhi wa-aḥwālī jalīlatun wa-anā wa-antum sawāʾun
sentences.l: and the inheritance that befell me with you, God has put blessing in it, and I pay zakāt on it, and my circumstances are grand, and I and you are alike.'
sentences.i: The inheritance that fell to me along with you, God has put blessing in it; I give alms from it, my circumstances are ample, and you and I are equals.'
sentences.n: أُزَكِّي عَلَيْهِ: she pays zakāt, the obligatory alms-tax on wealth, which shows that she is well off.

sentences.t: وَأَحْسَنْتُ لَهَا غَايَةَ الْإِحْسَانِ فَقَعَدَتْ عِنْدِي مُدَّةَ سَنَةٍ كَامِلَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-aḥsantu lahā ghāyata al-iḥsāni fa-qaʿadat ʿindī muddata sanatin kāmilatin
sentences.l: And I did good to her, the utmost of kindness, and she sat with me the period of a complete year.
sentences.i: I treated her with the utmost kindness, and she stayed with me a full year.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ اشْتَغَلَ خَاطِرُنَا عَلَى أُخْتِنَا الْأُخْرَى
sentences.tr: wa-qadi ishtaghala khāṭirunā ʿalā ukhtinā al-ukhrā
sentences.l: And our mind had become occupied over our other sister.
sentences.i: Meanwhile our thoughts had grown anxious for our other sister.

sentences.t: فِيهَا كَانَ قَلِيلًا إِلَّا وَجَاءَتْ بِزِيٍّ أَنْجَسِ مَا جَاءَتْ بِهِ الْأُخْتُ الْكَبِيرَةُ فَعَمِلْتُ مَعَهَا أَكْثَرَ مَا عَمِلْتُ مَعَ الْأُولَى وَبَقِيَ لَهُمَا مَالٌ مِنْ مَالِي
sentences.tr: fīhā kāna qalīlan illā wa-jāʾat bi-ziyyin anjasi mā jāʾat bihi al-ukhtu al-kabīratu fa-ʿamiltu maʿahā akthara mā ʿamiltu maʿa al-ūlā wa-baqiya lahumā mālun min mālī
sentences.l: In it it was little, except that she came in a garb filthiest-of what the elder sister came with; so I did with her more than what I did with the first, and there remained to the two of them money from my money.
sentences.i: It was not long before she too came, in a garb fouler than the one in which the elder sister had come; and I did more for her than I had done for the first. And there remained with the two of them some money of mine.
sentences.n: فِيهَا كَانَ قَلِيلًا is read as printed; the meaning is plainly 'it was not long before', and فِيهَا may be a slip for فَمَا ('and it was not'). The pattern 'it was little except that she came' is the usual way to say 'no sooner than'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا بَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ قَالَتْ لِي
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā baʿda muddatin qālat lī
sentences.l: Then indeed the two of them, after a period, she said to me:
sentences.i: Then, after a time, the two of them said to me,
sentences.n: قَالَتْ is singular although the subject is the two sisters; the edition does this more than once, and it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: يَا أُخْتَاهُ أَنَا نُرِيدُ الزَّوَاجَ إِذْ لَيْسَ لَنَا صَبْرٌ عَلَى الْقُعُودِ بِلَا زَوْجٍ
sentences.tr: yā ukhtāhu anā nurīdu al-zawāja idh laysa lanā ṣabrun ʿalā al-quʿūdi bi-lā zawjin
sentences.l: 'O my sister, I we-want marriage, since there is not for us patience for the sitting without a husband.'
sentences.i: 'Sister, we want to marry, for we have no patience to go on sitting without a husband.'
sentences.n: أَنَا نُرِيدُ pairs the singular pronoun 'I' with a plural verb ('we want'); the two women speak as one. The final هُ of أُخْتَاهُ is the pausal ending of the call 'O my sister!'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ يَا عُيُونِي مَا بَقِيَ فِي ازْدِوَاجٍ خَيْرٌ وَالْآنَ الرَّجُلُ الْجَمِيلُ عَزِيزُ الْوُجُودِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahum yā ʿuyūnī mā baqiya fī izdiwājin khayrun wa-al-āna al-rajulu al-jamīlu ʿazīzu al-wujūdi
sentences.l: So I said to them: 'O my eyes, there does not remain in marriage any good; and now the fine man is dear of finding.
sentences.i: I said to them, 'Dear ones, there is no good left in marriage; and nowadays a worthy man is hard to find.
sentences.n: يَا عُيُونِي, 'O my eyes', is a term of endearment. لَهُمْ is masculine plural ('to them') though it addresses two women. عَزِيزُ الْوُجُودِ, 'dear of finding', means rare.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَرَ فِيمَا ذَكَرْتُمْ صَلَاحًا وَأَنْتُمْ جَرَّبْتُمُ الزَّوَاجَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam ara fīmā dhakartum ṣalāḥan wa-antum jarrabtumu al-zawāja
sentences.l: And I do not see in what you mention any soundness, and you have tried marriage.'
sentences.i: I see no good in what you propose, and you have tried marriage for yourselves.'

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَتَقَبَّلُوا كَلَامِي وَتَزَوَّجُوا بِغَيْرِ رِضَائِي فَجَهَّزْتُهُمْ مِنْ مَالِي وَسَتَرْتُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yataqabbalū kalāmī wa-tazawwajū bi-ghayri riḍāʾī fa-jahhaztuhum min mālī wa-satartuhum
sentences.l: So they did not accept my speech, and they married without my consent; so I equipped them from my money, and I covered them.
sentences.i: But they would not take my counsel, and married without my consent; so I fitted them out from my own wealth and sheltered them.

sentences.t: وَمَضَوْا مَعَ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ فَقَعَدُوا مُدَّةً يَسِيرَةً وَلَعِبُوا عَلَيْهِمْ أَزْوَاجُهُمْ وَ أَخَذُوا مَاكَانَ مَعَهُمْ وَسَافَرُوا وَتَرَكُوهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-maḍaw maʿa azwājihim fa-qaʿadū muddatan yasīratan wa-laʿibū ʿalayhim azwājuhum wa-akhadhū mā kāna maʿahum wa-sāfarū wa-tarakūhum
sentences.l: And they went off with their husbands, and they stayed a short while, and they played upon them, their husbands, and they took what was with them, and they travelled, and they left them.
sentences.i: They went off with their husbands and stayed a short while; then the husbands tricked them, took everything they had, and travelled away, leaving them behind.
sentences.n: وَلَعِبُوا عَلَيْهِمْ أَزْوَاجُهُمْ: the verb agrees in the plural with a subject that follows it (Classical would say لَعِبَ), a common Middle Arabic pattern. لَعِبَ عَلَى is 'to play upon, to cheat'.

sentences.t: فَجَاءُوا عِنْدِي وَهُمْ خَزَايَا وَ اعْتَذَرُوا وَقَالُوا
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾū ʿindī wa-hum khazāyā wa-aʿtadharū wa-qālū
sentences.l: So they came to my place, and they abashed, and they made excuse, and they said:
sentences.i: So they came back to me, abashed, and made their excuses, saying:

sentences.t: لَا تُؤَاخِذِينَا فَأَنْتِ أَصْغَرُ مِنَّا سِنًّا وَأَكْمَلُ عَقْلًا وَمَابَقِينَا نَذْكُرُ إِلَّا زَوَاجَ أَبَدًا فَاتَّخِذِينَا جَوَارِيَ عِنْدَكِ نَأْكُلُ لُقْمَتَنَا
sentences.tr: lā tuʾākhidhīnā fa-anti aṣgharu minnā sinnan wa-akmalu ʿaqlan wa-mā baqīnā nadhkuru illā zawāja abadan fa-ittakhidhīnā jawāriya ʿindaki naʾkulu luqmatanā
sentences.l: Do not hold us to account, for you are smaller than us in age and more complete in mind, and we no longer remain mentioning except marriage, ever; so take us as slave-girls at your place; we eat our morsel.
sentences.i: Do not blame us; you are younger than we are, yet fuller in wisdom. We shall never speak of marriage again. Take us as handmaids in your house, and we will eat our bit of bread.
sentences.n: وَمَابَقِينَا نَذْكُرُ إِلَّا زَوَاجَ أَبَدًا is printed as it stands, with إِلَّا 'except'; the sense wanted is plainly 'we will never mention marriage again', so the إِلَّا is odd, and it may be a printing slip for a plain negative. Read here as printed, with the translation following the sense. Note also the Middle Arabic use of مَا بَقِينَا + present verb for 'no longer'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ مَرْحَبًا بِكُمْ يَا أَخَوَاتِي مَا عِنْدِي أَعَزُّ مِنْكُمْ وَقَبِلْتُهُمْ وَزِدْتُهُمْ إِكْرَامًا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu marḥaban bikum yā akhawātī mā ʿindī aʿazzu minkum wa-qabiltuhum wa-zidtuhum ikrāman
sentences.l: So I said: 'Welcome with you, O my sisters; there is not at my place anyone dearer than you.' And I accepted them, and I increased them in honour.
sentences.i: I said, 'Welcome, my sisters; nothing I have is dearer to me than you.' So I received them and showed them still more honour.
sentences.n: بِكُمْ, مِنْكُمْ, وَقَبِلْتُهُمْ: the masculine plural pronoun is used for the sisters, where Classical would use feminine ـكُنَّ / ـهُنَّ; this is regular Middle Arabic and is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ نَزَلْ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ سَنَةً كَامِلَةً فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُجَهِّزَ لِي مَرْكَبًا إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam nazal ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati sanatan kāmilatan fa-aradtu an ujahhiza lī markaban ilā al-baṣrati
sentences.l: And we did not cease upon this state a complete year; so I wished to equip for myself a ship to al-Basra.
sentences.i: We remained in this state a whole year; then I wished to fit out a ship for myself, bound for Basra.

sentences.t: فَجَهَّزْتُ مَرْكَبًا كَبِيرًا وَحَمَلْتُ فِيهَا الْبَضَائِعَ وَالْمَتَاجِرَ وَمَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْمَرْكَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-jahhaztu markaban kabīran wa-ḥamaltu fīhā al-baḍāʾiʿa wa-al-matājira wa-mā naḥtāju ilayhi fī al-markabi
sentences.l: So I equipped a large ship, and I loaded in it the wares and the trade-goods and what we need of it in the ship.
sentences.i: So I fitted out a large ship and loaded her with wares and merchandise, and with all we should need on board.
sentences.n: The ship is treated as feminine here (فِيهَا) and elsewhere in the night as masculine or feminine as suits the clause; مَرْكَب takes either.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ يَا أَخَوَاتِي هَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَقْعُدُوا فِى الْمَنْزِلِ حَتَّى أُسَافِرَ وَأَرْجِعَ أَوْ تَأْنُوا مَعِي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu yā akhawātī hal lakum an taqʿudū fī al-manzili ḥattā usāfira wa-arjiʿa aw taʾnū maʿī
sentences.l: And I said: 'O my sisters, is there for you that you sit in the house until I travel and return, or you ...-ing with me?'
sentences.i: I said, 'My sisters, would you rather stay at home until I have travelled and returned, or come along with me?'
sentences.n: أَوْ تَأْنُوا مَعِي: the printed تأنوا is the puzzle of this line. The sense requires 'or come with me', which would be تَأْتُوا; the letters printed have ن for ت, a slip of the same kind as elsewhere in this text. It is vocalised as printed, and the translation follows the sense. (Read as a real verb from أَنَى, it would mean 'be slow, be patient', which does not suit the sentence as well.)

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا نُسَافِرُ مَعَكَ فَإِنَّا لَا نُطِيقُ فِرَاقَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū nusāfiru maʿaka fa-innā lā nuṭīqu firāqaka
sentences.l: So they said: 'We travel with you, for we do not endure your separation.'
sentences.i: They said, 'We will travel with you, for we cannot bear to be parted from you.'

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُهُمَا وَكُنْتُ قَسَمْتُ مَالِي نِصْفَيْنِ أَخَذْتُ النِّصْفَ وَالنِّصْفُ الثَّانِي أَوْدَعْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtuhumā wa-kuntu qasamtu mālī niṣfayni akhadhtu al-niṣfa wa-al-niṣfu al-thānī awdaʿtuhu
sentences.l: So I took the two of them; and I had divided my money into two halves: I took the half, and the second half, I deposited it.
sentences.i: So I took them both. I had divided my wealth in two: I took one half with me and left the other half on deposit.
sentences.n: فَأَخَذْتُهُمَا has the dual 'both of them' though two sisters are meant with the plural pronoun elsewhere; the text is not consistent. وَالنِّصْفُ الثَّانِي أَوْدَعْتُهُ puts the object first as a topic and resumes it with the pronoun ـهُ.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ رُبَّمَا يُصِيبُ الْمَرْكَبَ شَيْءٌ وَيَكُونُ فِى الْعُمْرِ مُدَّةٌ فَإِذَا رَجَعْنَا نَجِدُ شَيْئًا يَنْفَعُنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qultu rubbamā yuṣību al-markaba shayʾun wa-yakūnu fī al-ʿumri muddatun fa-idhā rajaʿnā najidu shayʾan yanfaʿunā
sentences.l: And I said: 'Perhaps something befalls the ship, and there is in the life a span; so when we return we find something that benefits us.'
sentences.i: I said to myself, 'Something may befall the ship; and life may yet run on. Then, when we return, we shall find something to serve us.'

sentences.t: وَسَافَرْنَا أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ تَلَاطَمَتْ بِنَا الْمَرْكَبُ وَ غَفَلَ الرَّئِيسُ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ وَدَخَلَ الْمَرْكَبُ بَحْرًا غَيْرَ الْبَحْرِ الَّذِي نُرِيدُ؛
sentences.tr: wa-sāfarnā ayyāman wa-layāliya talāṭamat binā al-markabu wa-ghafala al-raʾīsu ʿani al-ṭarīqi wa-dakhala al-markabu baḥran ghayra al-baḥri alladhī nurīdu;
sentences.l: And we travelled days and nights; the ship tossed with us, and the captain was heedless of the way, and the ship entered a sea other than the sea which we want;
sentences.i: We sailed for days and nights; the ship was tossed about with us, and the captain lost his way, and the vessel passed into a sea other than the one we sought;
sentences.n: تَلَاطَمَتْ بِنَا الْمَرْكَبُ: the verb is feminine and the noun marked here with the masculine ending; the printed text treats مَرْكَب as either gender. تَلَاطَمَ بِنَا means literally 'it dashed (waves) with us'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ نَعْلَمْ ذَلِكَ مُدَّةً وَطَابَتْ لَنَا الرِّيحُ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَبَعْدَ عَشَرَةٍ طَلَعَ النَّاطُورُ يَنْظُرُ فَقَالَ الْبِشَارَةَ وَنَزَلَ وَهُوَ فَرْحَانُ وَقَالَ رَأَيْتُ صِفَةَ مَدِينَةٍ وَهِيَ مِثْلُ الْحَمَامَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam naʿlam dhālika muddatan wa-ṭābat lanā al-rīḥu ʿasharata ayyāmin wa-baʿda ʿasharatin ṭalaʿa al-nāṭūru yanẓuru fa-qāla al-bishārata wa-nazala wa-huwa farḥānu wa-qāla raʾaytu ṣifata madīnatin wa-hiya mithlu al-ḥamāmati
sentences.l: And we did not know that for a while, and the wind was good for us ten days, and after ten the lookout went up looking; then he said: 'The glad tidings!' and he came down, and he was joyful, and he said: 'I saw the look of a city, and it is like the dove.'
sentences.i: For a time we did not know it. The wind stayed fair for ten days; then the lookout climbed up to scan the sea, and cried, 'Good news!' He came down rejoicing and said, 'I have seen the shape of a city, and it looks like a dove.'
sentences.n: وَهِيَ مِثْلُ الْحَمَامَةِ: 'like the dove' is left as printed; the sense is presumably that the city looks white and small like a dove in the distance, but the text does not say.

sentences.t: فَرِحْنَا وَمَا مَرَّتْ عَلَيْنَا سَاعَةٌ مِنَ النَّهَارِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ لَاحَتْ لَنَا مَدِينَةٌ عَلَى بُعْدٍ
sentences.tr: fariḥnā wa-mā marrat ʿalaynā sāʿatun mina al-nahāri illā wa-qad lāḥat lanā madīnatun ʿalā buʿdin
sentences.l: We rejoiced; and there did not pass over us an hour of the day but that a city had appeared to us at a distance.
sentences.i: We rejoiced; and hardly an hour of the day had passed before a city came into view, far off.

sentences.t: فَقُلْنَا لِلرَّئِيسِ مَا اسْمُ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ الَّتِي أَشْرَفْنَا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qulnā li-al-raʾīsi mā ismu hādhihi al-madīnati allatī ashrafnā ʿalayhā
sentences.l: So we said to the captain: 'What is the name of this city which we have overlooked?'
sentences.i: We said to the captain, 'What is the name of this city that we are coming upon?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَعْلَمُ وَلَا رَأَيْتُهَا قَطُّ وَلَا سَلَكْتُ عُمْرِي هَذَا الْبَحْرَ وَلَكِنْ جَاءَ الْأَمْرُ بِسَلَامَةٍ فَمَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةَ وَانْظُرُوا بَضَائِعَكُمْ فَإِنْ حَصَلَ لَكُمْ بَيْعٌ بِيعُوا وَتَسَوَّقُوا مَهْمَا كَانَ فِيهَا وَإِنْ لَمْ يَحْصُلْ لَكُمْ بَيْعٌ نَرْتَاحُ يَوْمَيْنِ وَنَتَزَوَّدُ وَنُسَافِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-allāhi lā aʿlamu wa-lā raʾaytuhā qaṭṭu wa-lā salaktu ʿumrī hādhā al-baḥra wa-lākin jāʾa al-amru bi-salāmatin fa-mā baqiya illā an tadkhulū hādhihi al-madīnata wa-unẓurū baḍāʾiʿakum fa-in ḥaṣala lakum bayʿun bīʿū wa-tasawwaqū mahmā kāna fīhā wa-in lam yaḥṣul lakum bayʿun nartāḥu yawmayni wa-natazawwadu wa-nusāfiru
sentences.l: So he said: 'By God, I do not know, and I have never seen it, and I have not sailed, in this my life, this sea; but the matter has come with safety, so nothing remains but that you enter this city, and you look to your wares; and if a sale comes about for you, sell, and trade whatever there is in it; and if no sale comes about for you, we rest two days, and we take provisions, and we travel.'
sentences.i: He said, 'By God, I do not know it; I have never seen it, nor in all my life have I sailed this sea. Still, we have come here safely, so nothing remains but for you to enter this city and see to your wares. If you can sell, sell, and buy up whatever it holds; and if there is no selling for you, we shall rest two days, take on provisions, and sail on.'
sentences.n: وَانْظُرُوا is an imperative continuing after أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا, where Classical Arabic would keep the subjunctive (وَتَنْظُرُوا); the shift of mood is a Middle Arabic looseness, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ وَطَلَعَ الرَّئِيسُ إِلَيْهَا وَ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalnā al-madīnata wa-ṭalaʿa al-raʾīsu ilayhā wa-
sentences.l: So we entered the city, and the captain went up to it, and ...
sentences.i: We entered the city, and the captain went up to it as well, and
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off here with a bare وَ at the end of the printed line; it continues in the next sentence.

sentences.t: غَابَ سَاعَةً وَأتَى إلَيْنَا وَقَالَ قُومُوا اُطْلُعُوا إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَتَعَجَّبُوا فِي صُنْعِ اللَّهِ فِي خَلْقِهِ وَاسْتَعِيذُوا مِنْ سَخَطِهِ
sentences.tr: ghāba sāʿatan wa-atā ilaynā wa-qāla qūmū uṭluʿū ilā al-madīnati wa-taʿajjabū fī ṣunʿi allāhi fī khalqihi wa-istaʿīdhū min sakhaṭihi
sentences.l: He was gone an hour, and came to us and said, 'Rise, go up to the city, and marvel at the making of God in His creation, and seek refuge from His wrath.'
sentences.i: He was gone for an hour, then came back to us and said, 'Arise and go up into the city. Marvel at what God has wrought in His creation, and take refuge in Him from His wrath.'

sentences.t: فَطَلَعْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ فَلَمَّا أتَيْتُ الْبَابَ رَأَيْتُ أنَاسًا بِأَيْدِيهِمْ عِصِيٌّ عَلَى بَابِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَدَنَوْتُ مِنْهُمْ وَإذَا هُمْ مَسْخُوطِينَ وَقَدْ صَارُوا أَحْجَارًا
sentences.tr: faṭalaʿnā al-madīnata fa-lammā ataytu al-bāba raʾaytu unāsan bi-aydīhim ʿiṣiyyun ʿalā bābi al-madīnati fa-danawtu minhum wa-idhā hum maskhūṭīna wa-qad ṣārū aḥjāran
sentences.l: So we went-up the city; and when I came the gate I saw people, in their hands staves, at the gate of the city; so I drew near from them, and behold, they (were) cursed-ones, and they had become stones.
sentences.i: So we went up into the city, and when I reached the gate I saw people with staves in their hands standing at the city gate. I drew near them, and behold, they had been smitten with a curse and turned to stones.
sentences.n: مَسْخُوطِينَ after وَإِذَا هُمْ is printed in the oblique plural where Classical Arabic would have the nominative مَسْخُوطُونَ; a Middle Arabic habit kept as printed. مَسْخُوط is 'cursed, made the object of wrath' and is the word the tale uses for those turned to stone. أَتَيْتُ الْبَابَ takes the gate directly, without a preposition.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ فَوَجَدْنَا كُلَّ مَنْ فِيهَا مَسْخُوطًا أَحْجَارًا سُودًا لَا فِيهَا دِيَارٌ وَلَا نَافِخُ نَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalnā al-madīnata fa-wajadnā kulla man fīhā maskhūṭan aḥjāran sūdan lā fīhā diyārun wa-lā nāfikhu nārin
sentences.l: So we entered the city, and we found every-one who (was) in it cursed, stones, black; not in it (any) dweller, and not a blower-of-fire.
sentences.i: We entered the city and found everyone in it cursed and turned to black stones; there was not a soul in its houses, not one to blow a fire.
sentences.n: لَا فِيهَا دِيَارٌ وَلَا نَافِخُ نَارٍ is a proverbial way of saying 'no one at all': 'no dweller and no fire-blower' (that is, no one to kindle a fire in a hearth). دِيَار here means an inhabitant of the dwellings, as in the idiom لَيْسَ بِالدَّارِ دَيَّارٌ.

sentences.t: فَانْدَهَشْنَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَشَقَقْنَا الْأَسْوَاقَ فَوَجَدْنَا الْبَضَائِعَ بَاقِيَةً وَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ بَاقِيَةً عَلَى حَالِهَا فَتَعَجَّبْنَا وَقُلْنَا لَعَلَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِهَذَا شَأْنٌ
sentences.tr: fa-andahashnā min dhālika fa-shaqaqnā al-aswāqa fa-wajadnā al-baḍāʾiʿa bāqiyatan wa-al-dhahaba wa-al-fiḍḍata bāqiyatan ʿalā ḥālihā fa-taʿajjabnā wa-qulnā laʿalla an yakūna li-hādhā shaʾnun
sentences.l: So we were bewildered from that, and we clove the markets, and we found the wares remaining, and the gold and the silver remaining upon their state; so we marvelled, and we said, 'Perhaps that it be for this a matter.'
sentences.i: We were astounded at this. We passed through the markets and found the merchandise still in place, and the gold and silver untouched, just as they were. We marvelled, and said, 'Perhaps there is some reason behind all this.'
sentences.n: لَعَلَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ is not Classical (لَعَلَّ normally takes a noun in the accusative, not أَنْ + verb); it is a Middle Arabic construction, kept as printed. شَأْنٌ ('matter, concern') is left deliberately open: the men suspect that some cause lies behind the disaster.

sentences.t: فَتَفَرَّقْنَا فِي شَوَارِعِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ اشْتَغَلَ عَنْ رَفِيقِهِ بِالْكَسْبِ وَالْمَالِ وَالْقُمَاشِ
sentences.tr: fa-tafarraqnā fī shawāriʿi al-madīnati wa-kullu wāḥidin ishtaghala ʿan rafīqihi bi-al-kasbi wa-al-māli wa-al-qumāshi
sentences.l: So we dispersed in the streets of the city, and each one busied-himself away-from his companion with the gain and the wealth and the cloth.
sentences.i: So we scattered through the streets of the city, and each man, forgetting his companion, busied himself with gathering gain, money and fine stuffs.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَنَا فَطَلَعْتُ إلَى الْقَلْعَةِ فَوَجَدْتُهَا مُحْكَمَةً فَدَخَلْتُ قَصْرَ الْمَلِكِ فَوَجَدْتُ جَمِيعَ الْأَوَانِي مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَ الْفِضَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā anā faṭalaʿtu ilā al-qalʿati fa-wajadtuhā muḥkamatan fa-dakhaltu qaṣra al-maliki fa-wajadtu jamīʿa al-awānī mina al-dhahabi wa-al-fiḍḍati
sentences.l: And as-for me, I went-up to the citadel, and I found it strongly-built, and I entered the palace of the king, and I found all the vessels of gold and of silver.
sentences.i: As for me, I climbed to the citadel and found it strongly fortified. I entered the king's palace and found all its vessels to be of gold and silver.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ رَأَيْتُ الْمَلِكَ جَالِسًا وَعِنْدَهُ حُجَّابُهُ وَنُوَّابُهُ وَوُزَرَاؤُهُ وَعَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَلَابِسِ شَيْءٌ يُحَيِّرُ فِيهِ الْفِكْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika raʾaytu al-malika jālisan wa-ʿindahu ḥujjābuhu wa-nuwwābuhu wa-wuzarāʾuhu wa-ʿalayhi mina al-malābisi shayʾun yuḥayyiru fīhi al-fikru
sentences.l: So at that I saw the king sitting, and with him his chamberlains and his deputies and his viziers, and upon him, of the garments, a thing in which thought is bewildered.
sentences.i: Then I saw the king seated, with his chamberlains, his deputies and his viziers about him, and he wore such raiment as leaves the mind bewildered.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَدِمْتُ إلَى الْمَلِكِ وَجَدْتُهُ جَالِسًا عَلَى كُرْسِيٍّ مُرَصَّعٍ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ عَلَيْهِ بَدْلَةٌ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَفِيهِ كُلُّ جَوْهَرَةٍ تُضِيءُ مِثْلَ النَّجْمَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qadimtu ilā al-maliki wajadtuhu jālisan ʿalā kursiyyin muraṣṣaʿin bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari ʿalayhi badlatun mina al-dhahabi wa-fīhi kullu jawharatin tuḍīʾu mithla al-najmati
sentences.l: And when I came-forward to the king, I found him sitting upon a throne inlaid with pearls and jewels; upon him a suit of gold, and in it every jewel shining like the star.
sentences.i: When I came before the king, I found him seated on a throne set with pearls and jewels, wearing a suit of cloth of gold, and every jewel in it shone like a star.
sentences.n: وَفِيهِ refers back to the suit (بَدْلَة): the jewels are set in his golden garment.

sentences.t: وَوَاقِفٌ حَوْلَهُ خَمْسُونَ مَمْلُوكًا لَابِسِينَ أَنْوَاعَ الْحَرِيرِ وَفِي أَيْدِيهِمُ السُّيُوفُ مُجَرَّدَةً
sentences.tr: wa-wāqifun ḥawlahu khamsūna mamlūkan lābisīna anwāʿa al-ḥarīri wa-fī aydīhimu al-suyūfu mujarradatan
sentences.l: And standing around him fifty slaves, wearing kinds of silk, and in their hands the swords, drawn.
sentences.i: Around him stood fifty mamluks clad in every kind of silk, with drawn swords in their hands.
sentences.n: مَمْلُوك ('owned one') is the military slave of the sultan's guard, a mamluk. وَاقِفٌ is singular before its plural subject, as is regular when the participle comes first.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرْتُ ذَلِكَ دَهِشَ عَقْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓartu dhālika dahisha ʿaqlī
sentences.l: And when I looked (at) that, my mind was bewildered.
sentences.i: At that sight my wits were dazed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَشَيْتُ وَدَخَلْتُ قَاعَةَ الْحَرِيمِ فَوَجَدْتُ فِي حِيطَانِهَا سَتَائِرَ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ مَنْقُوشَةً بِقُضْبَانِ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma mashaytu wa-dakhaltu qāʿata al-ḥarīmi fa-wajadtu fī ḥīṭānihā satāʾira mina al-ḥarīri manqūshatan bi-quḍbāni al-dhahabi
sentences.l: Then I walked, and I entered the hall of the harem, and I found in its walls curtains of silk, embroidered with rods of gold.
sentences.i: Then I walked on and entered the harem hall, and found on its walls curtains of silk embroidered with rods of gold.

sentences.t: وَوَجَدْتُ الْمَلِكَةَ نَائِمَةً وَعَلَيْهَا بَدْلَةٌ مِنَ اللُّؤْلُؤِ الرَّطْبِ وَعَلَى رَأْسِهَا تَاجٌ مُكَلَّلٌ بِأَنْوَاعِ الْفُصُوصِ وَ فِي عُنُقِهَا قَلَائِدُ وَعُقُودٌ وَجَمِيعُ مَا عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْمَلْبُوسِ وَالْمَصَاغِ عَلَى حَالِهِ وَهِيَ مَسْخُوطَةٌ حَجَرًا أَسْوَدَ
sentences.tr: wa-wajadtu al-malikata nāʾimatan wa-ʿalayhā badlatun mina al-luʾluʾi al-raṭbi wa-ʿalā raʾsihā tājun mukallalun bi-anwāʿi al-fuṣūṣi wa-fī ʿunuqihā qalāʾidu wa-ʿuqūdun wa-jamīʿu mā ʿalayhā mina al-malbūsi wa-al-maṣāghi ʿalā ḥālihi wa-hiya maskhūṭatun ḥajaran aswada
sentences.l: And I found the queen sleeping, and upon her a suit of fresh pearls, and upon her head a crown crowned with kinds of gems, and on her neck necklaces and collars, and all that (was) upon her of the worn-things and the jewellery (was) upon its state; and she (was) cursed, a stone, black.
sentences.i: I found the queen lying asleep, wearing a suit of fresh pearls, and upon her head a crown set with every kind of gem, and about her neck necklaces and collars. All that she wore, her clothes and her jewels, lay just as it was; but she herself had been cursed and turned to a black stone.
sentences.n: اللُّؤْلُؤ الرَّطْب, 'moist pearls', means freshly-lustrous pearls. حَالِهِ is masculine although its subject is جَمِيعُ (masculine, 'all'): the agreement is with 'all', not with the queen.

sentences.t: وَوَجَدْتُ بَابًا مَفْتُوحًا فَصَعِدْتُ إلَيْهِ وَهُوَ مَكَانٌ بِسَبْعِ دَرَجٍ فَوَجَدْتُهُ مَوْضِعٌ مُرَخَّمٌ مَفْرُوشٌ بِالْبُسُطِ الْمُذَهَّبَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-wajadtu bāban maftūḥan faṣaʿidtu ilayhi wa-huwa makānun bi-sabʿi darajin fa-wajadtuhu mawḍiʿun murakhkhamun mafrūshun bi-al-busuṭi al-mudhahhabati
sentences.l: And I found a door open, and I went-up to it, and it (was) a place with seven steps, and I found it a place, marble-paved, spread with the gilded carpets.
sentences.i: I found a door standing open and climbed up to it: it was a place reached by seven steps, and I found it a marble-paved chamber spread with gilded carpets.
sentences.n: فَوَجَدْتُهُ مَوْضِعٌ is printed without the accusative ending (Classical would be مَوْضِعًا); the nominative is kept as printed. مُرَخَّم means paved with marble.

sentences.t: وَوَجَدْتُ فِيهِ سَرِيرًا مِنَ الْعَرْعَرِ مُرَصَّعٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ وَ رُمَّانَيْنِ مِنَ الزُّمُرُّدِ وَعَلَيْهِ بَشْخَانَةٌ مُرْخِيَةٌ مَنْظُومَةٌ بِاللُّؤْلُؤِ
sentences.tr: wa-wajadtu fīhi sarīran mina al-ʿarʿari muraṣṣaʿun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari wa-rummānayni mina al-zumurrudi wa-ʿalayhi bashkhānatun murkhiyatun manẓūmatun bi-al-luʾluʾi
sentences.l: And I found in it a bed of juniper-wood, inlaid with pearls and jewels and two pomegranates of emerald; and upon it a canopy let-down, strung with pearls.
sentences.i: In it I found a bed of juniper wood set with pearls and jewels and two emerald pomegranates, and over it a canopy hung with strings of pearls.
sentences.n: بَشْخَانَة (a canopy or curtained alcove over a bed, from Persian) is a word of the Egyptian period. مُرَصَّعٌ is printed without the alif of the accusative (Classical would be مُرَصَّعًا) and is read as printed. رُمَّانَيْنِ is printed in the dual oblique and is read as another thing the bed is inlaid with.

sentences.t: وَنَظَرْتُ نُورًا خَارِجًا مِنْ بَابِ الْبَشْخَانَةِ فَطَلَعْتُ فَوْقَهُ فَوَجَدْتُ جَوْهَرَةً قَدْرَ بَيْضَةِ الْأَوَزَّةِ فِي صَدْرِ الْبَشْخَانَةِ عَلَى كُرْسِيٍّ صَغِيرٍ وَهُوَ يُوقِدُ كَالشَّمْعَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-naẓartu nūran khārijan min bābi al-bashkhānati faṭalaʿtu fawqahu fa-wajadtu jawharatan qadra bayḍati al-awazzati fī ṣadri al-bashkhānati ʿalā kursiyyin ṣaghīrin wa-huwa yūqidu ka-al-shamʿati
sentences.l: And I looked (at) a light going-out from the door of the canopy, so I went-up above it, and I found a jewel the measure of the egg of the goose in the chest of the canopy upon a small chair, and it blazes like the candle.
sentences.i: I saw a light shining from the opening of the canopy, and climbing up above it I found a jewel the size of a goose's egg, set at the head of the canopy on a small stool, blazing like a candle.
sentences.n: صَدْر ('chest') is here the upper end, the 'head', of the canopy.

sentences.t: وَنُورُهَا سَاطِعٌ وَمَفْرُوشٌ عَلَى ذَلِكَ السَّرِيرِ مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْحَرِيرِ مَا يُحَيِّرُ النَّاظِرَ
sentences.tr: wa-nūruhā sāṭiʿun wa-mafrūshun ʿalā dhālika al-sarīri min anwāʿi al-ḥarīri mā yuḥayyiru al-nāẓira
sentences.l: And its light (was) radiant, and spread upon that bed, of kinds of silk, what bewilders the looker.
sentences.i: Its light was dazzling, and spread upon that bed were silks of such kinds as bewilder the beholder.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرْتُ ذَلِكَ تَعَجَّبْتُ وَرَأَيْتُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ شُمُوعًا مُوقَدَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓartu dhālika taʿajjabtu wa-raʾaytu fī dhālika al-makāni shumūʿan mūqadatan
sentences.l: So when I saw that, I marvelled, and I saw in that place candles lit.
sentences.i: When I saw this I marvelled, and in that place I saw candles burning.
sentences.n: شُمُوعًا مُوقَدَةً: the adjective is feminine singular, the regular Arabic agreement for a plural of things.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَابُدَّ أَنَّ أَحَدًا أَوْقَدَ هَذِهِ الشُّمُوعَ ثُمَّ إِنِّي مَشَيْتُ وَدَخَلْتُ إِلَى مَوْضِعٍ غَيْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā budda anna aḥadan awqada hādhihi al-shumūʿa thumma innī mashaytu wa-dakhaltu ilā mawḍiʿin ghayrihi
sentences.l: So I said, 'There is no escape (from it): someone has lit these candles.' Then I walked, and I entered into a place other-than-it.
sentences.i: I said to myself, 'Someone must have lit these candles.' Then I walked on and entered another place.
sentences.n: لَابُدَّ is printed as a single word; it is the fixed phrase 'there is no escape (from it)', i.e. 'it must be that'.

sentences.t: وَصِرْتُ أُفَتِّشُ وَأَدُورُ فِي الْأَمَاكِنِ وَنَسِيتُ نَفْسِي مِمَّا لَحِقَنِي مِنَ الْعَجَبِ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْأَحْوَالِ وَغَرِقْتُ فِي فِكْرِي إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣirtu ufattishu wa-adūru fī al-amākini wa-nasītu nafsī mimmā laḥiqanī min al-ʿajabi min tilka al-aḥwāli wa-ghariqtu fī fikrī ilā an dakhala al-laylu
sentences.l: And I began to search and to go around in the places, and I forgot myself from what overtook me of the wonder at those states-of-affairs, and I sank in my thought until the night entered.
sentences.i: I went searching and wandering through the rooms, and so amazed was I at those strange sights that I forgot myself, and lost myself in thought until night had fallen.
sentences.n: مِمَّا لَحِقَنِي مِنَ الْعَجَبِ: 'from what overtook me of wonder'; the verb لَحِقَ 'overtake, befall' is used for feelings that seize a person.

sentences.t: فَأَرَدْتُ الْخُرُوجَ فَلَمْ أَعْرِفِ الْبَابَ وَتِهْتُ فَعُدْتُ إِلَى الْبَشْخَانَةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الشَّمْعُ مَوْقُودٌ وَجَلَسْتُ عَلَى السَّرِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-aradtu al-khurūja fa-lam aʿrifi al-bāba wa-tihtu fa-ʿudtu ilā al-bashkhānati allatī fīhā al-shamʿu mawqūdun wa-jalastu ʿalā al-sarīri
sentences.l: So I wanted the going-out, and I did not know the door, and I lost my way; so I returned to the alcove in which the candles were lit, and I sat on the couch.
sentences.i: I wished to go out, but I could not find the door and lost my way; so I went back to the alcove where the candles were burning, and sat down upon the couch.
sentences.n: الشَّمْعُ مَوْقُودٌ: the collective noun الشَّمْع 'the candles' takes a singular masculine predicate, as is usual with collectives; earlier the plural شُمُوع took a feminine singular adjective.

sentences.t: وَتَغَطَّيْتُ بِلِحَافٍ بَعْدَ أَنْ قَرَأْتُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ وَأَرَدْتُ النَّوْمَ فَلَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ وَلَحِقَنِي الْقَلَقُ
sentences.tr: wa-taghaṭṭaytu bi-liḥāfin baʿda an qaraʾtu shayʾan min al-qurʾāni wa-aradtu al-nawma fa-lam astaṭiʿ wa-laḥiqanī al-qalaqu
sentences.l: And I covered myself with a quilt, after I had read something of the Qurʾān; and I wanted sleep, but I was not able, and restlessness overtook me.
sentences.i: I wrapped myself in a quilt, having read a little of the Qurʾān, and I wished to sleep but could not, for restlessness had seized me.
sentences.n: فَلَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ: the printed لَمْ is followed by a bare imperfect, so it is read as a jussive with the final vowel dropped: 'I was not able'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْتَصَفَ اللَّيْلُ سَمِعْتُ تِلَاوَةَ الْقُرْآنِ بِصَوْتٍ حَسَنٍ لَكِنَّهُ ضَعِيفُ الصَّوْتِ فَفَرِحْتُ وَتَبِعْتُ الصَّوْتَ إِلَى أَنْ جِئْتُ إِلَى مَخْدَعٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā intaṣafa al-laylu samiʿtu tilāwata al-qurʾāni bi-ṣawtin ḥasanin lākinnahu ḍaʿīfu al-ṣawti fa-fariḥtu wa-tabiʿtu al-ṣawta ilā an jiʾtu ilā makhdaʿin
sentences.l: So when the night reached its middle, I heard the recitation of the Qurʾān in a good voice, but faint-of-voice; so I rejoiced, and I followed the voice until I came to a small chamber.
sentences.i: When the night was half spent, I heard the Qurʾān being recited in a fair voice, though a faint one; I rejoiced and followed the sound until I came to a small chamber.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ بَابَهُ مَرْدُودًا فَفَتَحْتُ الْبَابَ وَنَظَرْتُ الْمَكَانَ فَإِذَا هُوَ مَعْبَدٌ وَمِحْرَابٌ وَفِيهِ قَنَادِيلُ مُعَلَّقَةٌ مَوْقُودَةٌ وَشَمْعَتَانِ وَفِيهِ سَجَّادَةٌ مَفْرُوشَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu bābahu mardūdan fa-fataḥtu al-bāba wa-naẓartu al-makāna fa-idhā huwa maʿbadun wa-miḥrābun wa-fīhi qanādīlu muʿallaqatun mawqūdatun wa-shamʿatāni wa-fīhi sajjādatun mafrūshatun
sentences.l: So I saw its door pushed-to; so I opened the door, and I looked at the place, and behold, it was a place-of-worship and a prayer-niche, and in it hung lamps, lit, and two candles, and in it a prayer-rug spread out,
sentences.i: I saw its door standing ajar, and I opened it and looked in, and behold, it was a place of worship with a prayer-niche, hung with lit lamps and with two candles, and a prayer-rug spread out in it,
sentences.n: فَإِذَا هُوَ: إِذَا here is the 'behold' of sudden discovery and does not mean 'if' or 'when'.

sentences.t: وَعَلَيْهَا شَابٌّ جَالِسٌ حَسَنُ الْمَنْظَرِ وَقُدَّامَهُ خَتْمَةٌ مُكَرَّسَةٌ وَهُوَ يَقْرَأُ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿalayhā shābbun jālisun ḥasanu al-manẓari wa-quddāmahu khatmatun mukarrasatun wa-huwa yaqraʾu
sentences.l: and on it a youth sitting, fair-of-appearance, and before him a complete Qurʾān in quires, and he was reading.
sentences.i: and upon it sat a comely youth, with a whole Qurʾān in bound quires before him, and he was reading.
sentences.n: خَتْمَةٌ is a complete copy of the Qurʾān, or one read through in full. مُكَرَّسَةٌ is obscure: I read it as 'made up in quires' (from كُرَّاسَة), but the meaning is not certain.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ كَيْفَ هُوَ سَالِمٌ دُونَ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَدَخَلْتُ وَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu kayfa huwa sālimun dūna ahli al-madīnati fa-dakhaltu wa-sallamtu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: So I marvelled how he was unharmed, apart from the people of the city; so I entered and I gave greeting on him.
sentences.i: I wondered how he alone, of all the people of the city, was safe; so I went in and gave him greeting.

sentences.t: فَرَفَعَ بَصَرَهُ وَرَدَّ عَلَيَّ السَّلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-rafaʿa baṣarahu wa-radda ʿalayya al-salāma
sentences.l: So he raised his gaze and returned to me the greeting.
sentences.i: He raised his eyes and returned my greeting.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَسْأَلُكَ بِحَقِّ مَا تَلَوْتَهُ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللهِ إِلَّا مَا أَجَبْتَنِي عَنْ سُؤَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu asʾaluka bi-ḥaqqi mā talawtahu min kitābi allāhi illā mā ajabtanī ʿan suʾālī
sentences.l: So I said to him, 'I ask you by the right of what you recited of the Book of God, that you answer me about my question.'
sentences.i: I said to him, 'I adjure you, by the right of what you have recited of the Book of God, to answer my question.'

sentences.t: وَالشَّابُّ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيَّ وَيَتَبَسَّمُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-shābbu yanẓuru ilayya wa-yatabassamu
sentences.l: And the youth was looking at me and smiling,
sentences.i: The youth looked at me, smiling,

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَيَّتُهَا الْأَمَةُ أَخْبِرِينِي أَنْتِ عَنْ سَبَبِ دُخُولِكِ هَذَا الْمَكَانَ وَأَنَا أُخْبِرُكِ بِمَا جَرَى عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَسَبَبِ خَلَاصِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ayyatuhā al-amatu akhbirīnī anti ʿan sababi dukhūliki hādhā al-makāna wa-anā ukhbiruki bi-mā jarā ʿalayya wa-ʿalā ahli hādhihi al-madīnati wa-sababi khalāṣī
sentences.l: and he said, 'O girl, tell me, you, about the reason of your entering this place, and I will tell you of what happened to me and to the people of this city, and the reason of my deliverance.'
sentences.i: and said, 'O maiden, first tell me why you have come into this place, and I will tell you what befell me and the people of this city, and how I was delivered.'

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِخَبَرِي فَتَعَجَّبَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ خَبَرِ أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhbartuhu bi-khabarī fa-taʿajjaba min dhālika thumma innī saʾaltuhu ʿan khabari ahli hādhihi al-madīnati
sentences.l: So I told him of my story, and he marvelled at that; then I asked him about the news of the people of this city.
sentences.i: So I told him my story, and he was astonished at it; then I asked him about the people of this city.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَمْهِلِينِي يَا أُخْتِي ثُمَّ طَبَّقَ الْخَتْمَةَ وَشَالَهَا فِي كِيسِ أَطْلَسٍ وَ أَجْلَسَنِي إِلَى جَانِبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla amhilīnī yā ukhtī thumma ṭabbaqa al-khatmata wa-shālahā fī kīsi aṭlasin wa- ajlasanī ilā jānibihi
sentences.l: So he said, 'Give me time, my sister.' Then he shut the Qurʾān-copy and lifted it into a satin bag, and seated me at his side.
sentences.i: He said, 'Give me a moment, my sister.' Then he closed the Qurʾān, put it away in a satin bag, and seated me beside him.
sentences.n: وَ is printed alone at the end of a line, apart from the أَجْلَسَنِي that follows it; it is a plain 'and', and is kept as printed. شَالَهَا 'lifted it' is colloquial (Classical حَمَلَهَا or رَفَعَهَا).

sentences.t: فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَإِذَا هُوَ كَالْبَدْرِ إِذَا بَدَرَ حَسَنُ الْأَوْصَافِ لَيِّنُ الْأَعْطَافِ حَسَنُ الْمَنْظَرِ كَأَنَّهُ قَالَبُ سُكَّرٍ مُعْتَدِلُ الْقَوَامِ كَمَا قِيلَ فِيهِ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓartu ilayhi fa-idhā huwa ka-al-badri idhā badara ḥasanu al-awṣāfi layyinu al-aʿṭāfi ḥasanu al-manẓari ka-annahu qālabu sukkarin muʿtadilu al-qawāmi ka-mā qīla fīhi hādhihi al-abyātu
sentences.l: So I looked at him, and behold, he was like the full moon when it rises full: fair of qualities, supple of flanks, fair of appearance, as though a block of sugar, well-proportioned of stature, as it was said of him in these verses.
sentences.i: I looked at him, and behold, he was like the full moon when it rises: fair in his qualities, supple in his bearing, fair to look upon, as though he were a block of sugar, shapely in stature, as it was said of him in these verses.
sentences.n: كَالْبَدْرِ إِذَا بَدَرَ: 'like the full moon when it is full'; the verb and the noun come from the same root (the pun is in the Arabic). The sentence ends by announcing verses, which the next piece of the night gives.

sentences.t:
رَصَدَ الْمُنَجِّمُ لَيْلَةً فَبَدَا لَهُ * قَلُّ الْمَلِيحِ يَلُوحُ فِي بُرْدَيْهِ
وَأَقَامَهُ زحلُ السوادِ بِشَعْرِهِ * وَحَبَاهُ لَوْنَ الْمِسْكِ فِي صُدْغَيْهِ
وَجَرَى مِنَ الْمِرِّيخِ حُمْرَةُ خَدِّهِ * وَالْقَوْسُ يَرْمِي النَّبْلَ مِنْ جَفْنَيْهِ
وَعُطَارِدُ أَعْطَاهُ فَرْطَ ذَكَائِهِ * وَأَبَى السُّهَا نَظَرَ الْوُشَاةِ إِلَيْهِ
فَبَقِيَ الْمُنَجِّمُ حَائِرًا لَمَّا رَأَى * وَالْبَدْرُ بَاسَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr:
raṣada al-munajjimu laylatan fa-badā lahu * qaddu al-malīḥi yalūḥu fī burdayhi
wa-aqāmahu zuḥalu al-sawādi bi-shaʿrihi * wa-ḥabāhu lawna al-miski fī ṣudghayhi
wa-jarā mina al-Mirrīkhi ḥumratu khaddihi * wa-al-qawsu yarmī al-nabla min jafnayhi
wa-ʿUṭāridu aʿṭāhu farṭa dhakāʾihi * wa-abā al-Suhā naẓara al-wushāti ilayhi
fa-baqiya al-munajjimu ḥāʾiran lammā raʾā * wa-al-badru bāsa al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l:
The astrologer kept watch one night, and there appeared to him * the stature of the handsome one, shining in his two mantles.
And Saturn of the blackness set it up with his hair * and endowed him with the colour of musk on his two temples.
And from Mars there ran the redness of his cheek * while the Bow shoots the arrow from his two eyelids.
And Mercury gave him the excess of his cleverness * and Suhā refused the gaze of the slanderers upon him.
So the astrologer remained bewildered when he saw * and the full-moon kissed the ground between his two hands.
sentences.i: One night the astrologer kept his watch, and there appeared the stature of the handsome one, shining in his two mantles. Saturn set it up with the blackness of his hair and gave him the hue of musk upon his temples; from Mars came the redness of his cheek, while the Bow shoots his arrows from his eyelids. Mercury bestowed on him a wealth of wit, and the star Suhā turned away the gaze of slanderers from him. The astrologer stood bewildered at what he saw, and the full moon kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: قَلُّ is printed with ل where the sense requires د: it is read as قَدُّ 'stature, figure' (the same ل/د slip seen elsewhere). زحلُ and السوادِ carry the edition's own printed vowels, which are kept as printed; with them زحلُ السوادِ reads 'Saturn of the blackness', i.e. Saturn as the planet of black. القوس 'the Bow' is Sagittarius, and السها is the faint star Suhā (Alcor) in the Great Bear, proverbially hard to see.

sentences.t: وَقَلْ أَلْبَسَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى حُلَّةَ الْكَمَالِ وَطَرَّزَهَا مِنْ عِذَارِهِ بِالْبَهَاءِ وَ الْجَمَالِ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad albasahu Allāhu taʿālā ḥullata al-kamāli wa-ṭarrazahā min ʿidhārihi bi-al-bahāʾi wa-al-jamāli ka-mā qāla fīhi al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And indeed God, exalted, clothed him with the robe of perfection and embroidered it, from his cheek-down, with radiance and beauty, just as the poet said of him:
sentences.i: God Most High had clothed him in the robe of perfection and embroidered it with radiance and beauty, from the first down upon his cheek, as the poet says of him:
sentences.n: وَقَلْ is printed with ل for د and is read وَقَدْ 'and indeed'. In the printed text a line ends after بالبهاء و and the next begins with الجمال; the two are read as one word, وَالْجَمَالِ, without changing a letter.

sentences.t:
قَسَمًا بِنَشْوَةِ جَفْنِهِ وَبِنَصْرِهِ * وَبَاسِمِهِ قَلْ رَاشَهَا مِنْ سِرِّهِ
وَبِلِينِ عِطْفَيْهِ وَمُرْهَفِ لَحْظِهِ * وَبَيَاضِ غُرَّتِهِ وَأَسْوَدِ شَعْرِهِ
وَبِحَاجِبٍ مَنَعَ الْكَرَي عَنْ نَاظِرِي * وَسَطَا عَلَىَّ بِنَهْيِهِ وَبِأَمْرِهِ
وَبِوَرْدِ خَدَّيْهِ وَآسِ عِذَارِهِ * وَعَقِيقِ مَبْسَمِهِ وَلُؤْلُؤِ ثَغْرِهِ
وَبِجِيدٍ وَبِحُسْنِ قَامَتِهِ الَّتِي * قَدْ أَطْلَعَتْ رَايَتَهُ فِي صَدْرِهِ
وَبِرِدْفِهِ الرَّجْرَجِ فِي حَرَكَاتِهِ * وَسُكُونِهِ وَبَرْقِهِ فِي خَصْرِهِ
وَحَرِيرِ مَلْمَسِهِ وَخِفَّةِ رُوحِهِ * وَبِمَا حَوَاهُ مِنَ الْجَمَالِ بِأَسْرِهِ
وَبِجُودِ رَاحَتِهِ وَصِدْقِ لِسَانِهِ * وَبِطِيبِ مَوْلِدِهِ وَعَالِي قَدْرِهِ
مَا الْمِسْكُ إِنْ عَرَفُوهُ إِلَّاعَرْفَهُ * وَالرِّيحُ عَنْبَرٌ نَشْرُهَا مِنْ نَشْرِهِ
وَكَذَٰلِكَ الشَّمْسُ الْمُنِيرَةُ دُونَهُ * مِمَّا حَكَتْهُ قُلَامَةٌ مِنْ ظُفْرِهِ
sentences.tr:
qasaman bi-nashwati jafnihi wa-bi-naṣrihi * wa-bi-bāsimihi qad rāshahā min sirrihi
wa-bi-līni ʿiṭfayhi wa-murhafi laḥẓihi * wa-bi-bayāḍi ghurratihi wa-aswadi shaʿrihi
wa-bi-ḥājibin manaʿa al-karā ʿan nāẓirī * wa-saṭā ʿalayya bi-nahyihi wa-bi-amrihi
wa-bi-wardi khaddayhi wa-āsi ʿidhārihi * wa-ʿaqīqi mabsamihi wa-luʾluʾi thaghrihi
wa-bi-jīdin wa-bi-ḥusni qāmatihi allatī * qad aṭlaʿat rāyatahu fī ṣadrihi
wa-bi-ridfihi al-rajraji fī ḥarakātihi * wa-sukūnihi wa-barqihi fī khaṣrihi
wa-ḥarīri malmasihi wa-khiffati rūḥihi * wa-bi-mā ḥawāhu mina al-jamāli bi-asrihi
wa-bi-jūdi rāḥatihi wa-ṣidqi lisānihi * wa-bi-ṭībi mawlidihi wa-ʿālī qadrihi
mā al-miskū in ʿarafūhu illā ʿarfahu * wa-al-rīḥu ʿanbarun nashruhā min nashrihi
wa-ka-dhālika al-shamsu al-munīratu dūnahu * mimmā ḥakathu qulāmatun min ẓufrihi
sentences.l:
An oath: by the intoxication of his eyelid and by his victory * and by his smiling one, which has feathered it from his secret,
And by the softness of his two flanks and the keen edge of his glance * and by the whiteness of his forehead and the blackest of his hair,
And by a brow that forbade sleep to my eye * and assaulted me with his prohibition and his command,
And by the rose of his two cheeks and the myrtle of his down * and the carnelian of his mouth and the pearl of his teeth,
And by a neck, and by the beauty of his stature, which * has raised his banner within his breast,
And by his quivering hindquarters in its movements * and its stillness, and his gleam at his waist,
And the silk of his touch and the lightness of his spirit * and by all that he holds of beauty, in its entirety,
And by the generosity of his palm and the truth of his tongue * and by the goodness of his birth and the loftiness of his rank:
Musk, if they knew it, is nothing but his fragrance * and the wind, ambergris being its scent, has its scent from his scent,
And likewise the shining sun is beneath him * of what a paring of his fingernail has imitated.
sentences.i: I swear by the languor of his eyelids and by his conquering power, and by his smile, which has, as it were, fledged them out of his secret; by the softness of his flanks and the keen edge of his glance, by the whiteness of his brow and the deep black of his hair; by a brow that kept sleep from my eyes and overpowered me with its forbidding and its bidding; by the rose of his cheeks and the myrtle of his down, the carnelian of his mouth and the pearl of his teeth; by his neck, and by the beauty of his stature, which has planted its banner in his breast; by his quivering buttocks in their motion and their rest, and the gleam at his waist; by the silk of his touch, the lightness of his spirit, and all the beauty that he holds entire; by the generosity of his hand, the truth of his tongue, the goodness of his birth and the height of his rank: musk, if men but knew it, is nothing but his fragrance, and the wind, whose scent is ambergris, takes its scent from his; and so too the shining sun is beneath him, matching no more than a paring of his fingernail.
sentences.n: This is one long oath, each line adding another 'by …' (وَبِـ), with the genitive carried on by bare وَ in وَحَرِيرِ and وَخِفَّةِ. Several words are printed with slips or run together, and each is read without changing a letter. قَلْ (here and in the verse above) is printed with ل for د and is read قَدْ, 'has indeed'. وَاسود is read وَأَسْوَدِ 'and the blackest of', and على is read عَلَيَّ 'upon me'. إِلَّاعَرْفَهُ is printed as one run, read إِلَّا عَرْفَهُ 'except his fragrance'. The first line is obscure: بِنَصْرِهِ is taken as 'by his victory' and رَاشَهَا as 'has feathered it' (as an arrow is fledged), but the referent of the pronoun is unclear and the wording may be corrupt. رَايَتَهُ 'his banner' is a plain reading, though رَأَيْتُهُ is conceivable.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرْتُ لَهُ نَظْرَةً أَعْقَبَتْنِي أَلْفَ حَسْرَةٍ وَتَعَلَّقَ قَلْبِي بِمَحَبَّتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓartu lahu naẓratan aʿqabatnī alfa ḥasratin wa-taʿallaqa qalbī bi-maḥabbatihi
sentences.l: So I looked at him a look that left-behind-me a thousand regrets, and my heart hung on his love.
sentences.i: I gazed at him, and that one glance left me a thousand regrets, and my heart clung to love of him.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا مَوْلَايَ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ مَا سَأَلْتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā mawlāya akhbirnī ʿan mā saʾaltuka
sentences.l: So I said to him, 'O my master, inform me about what I asked you.'
sentences.i: I said to him, 'My lord, tell me what I asked you.'
sentences.n: عَنْ مَا is printed as two words, 'about what'; classical usage would write عَمَّا. Kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً اعْلَمِي يَا أَمَةَ اللَّهِ أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةَ مَدِينَةُ وَالِدِي وَهُوَ الْمَلِكُ الَّذِي نَظَرْتِيهِ عَلَي الْكُرْسِيِّ وَ هُوَ حَجَرٌ أَسْوَدُ مَسْخُوطًا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan iʿlamī yā amata Allāhi anna hādhihi al-madīnata madīnatu wālidī wa-huwa al-maliku alladhī naẓartīhi ʿalā al-kursiyyi wa-huwa ḥajarun aswadu maskhūṭan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: So he said, 'Hearing and obedience. Know, O maidservant of God, that this city is the city of my father, and he is the king whom you-saw-him on the throne, and he is a black stone, made-the-object-of-wrath upon him.'
sentences.i: He said, 'With hearing and obedience. Know, servant of God, that this city is my father's city, and he is the king whom you saw on the throne, a black stone, under God's wrath.'
sentences.n: نَظَرْتِيهِ 'you (f.) saw him' keeps the ـي of the feminine -ti ending before the object suffix, and نَظَرَ is made to take a direct object; both are Middle Arabic and are kept as printed. أَسْوَدُ مَسْخُوطًا: the second word is accusative where classical Arabic would agree with حَجَرٌ (nominative); read as a circumstantial 'accursed as he is'.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْمَلِكَةُ الَّتِي قَدْ نَظَرْتِيهَا فِي الْبَشْخَانَةِ فَهِيَ أُمِّي وَجَمِيعُ أَهْلِهَا مَجُوسٌ يَعْبُدُونَ النَّارَ دُونَ الْمَلِكِ الْجَبَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-malikatu allatī qad naẓartīhā fī al-bashkhānati fa-hiya ummī wa-jamīʿu ahlihā majūsun yaʿbudūna al-nāra dūna al-maliki al-jabbāri
sentences.l: And as for the queen whom you-saw-her in the alcove, she is my mother; and all her people are Magians, they worship the fire, apart-from the King, the Almighty.
sentences.i: As for the queen whom you saw in the alcove, she is my mother; and all her people are Magians who worship fire instead of the King, the Almighty.
sentences.n: الْبَشْخَانَة is a Persian-derived word for a canopy or canopied alcove; the youth uses it loosely for the room where the girl saw his mother, and its exact sense here is uncertain.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ يُقْسِمُونَ بِالنَّارِ وَالنُّورِ وَالظِّلِّ وَالسُّرُورِ وَالْفَلَكِ الَّذِي يَدُورُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna yuqsimūna bi-al-nāri wa-al-nūri wa-al-ẓilli wa-al-surūri wa-al-falaki alladhī yadūru
sentences.l: And it-was they-swear by the fire and the light and the shade and the gladness and the sphere which revolves.
sentences.i: They swore by fire and light, by shade and gladness, and by the sphere that turns.
sentences.n: وَكَانَ is singular though the subject is plural (كَانُوا would be classical); a Middle Arabic habit kept as printed. The four oaths end in rhyme (النُّور، السُّرُور، يَدُور).

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَبِي لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَرُزِقَ بِي فِي آخِرِ عُمْرِهِ فَرَبَّانِي حَتَّى نَشَأْتُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna abī laysa lahu waladun wa-ruziqa bī fī ākhiri ʿumrihi fa-rabbānī ḥattā nashaʾtu
sentences.l: And my father, there-was-not to him a child, and he was provided-with me at the end of his life, and he raised me until I grew up.
sentences.i: My father had no child, and I was granted to him at the end of his life, and he brought me up until I was grown.

sentences.t: وَ قَدْ سَبَقَتْ لِيَ السَّعَادَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad sabaqat liya al-saʿādatu
sentences.l: And happiness had gone-before for me.
sentences.i: And good fortune had gone before me.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عِنْدَنَا عَجُوزٌ طَاعِنَةٌ فِي السِّنِّ مُسْلِمَةٌ تُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فِي الْبَاطِنِ وَتُوَافِقُ أَهْلِي فِي الظَّاهِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿindanā ʿajūzun ṭāʿinatun fī al-sinni muslimatun tuʾminu bi-Allāhi wa-rasūlihi fī al-bāṭini wa-tuwāfiqu ahlī fī al-ẓāhiri
sentences.l: And there-was with us an old woman, thrusting in age, a Muslim, who believed in God and his messenger in the inward, and agreed with my people in the outward.
sentences.i: We had with us an aged woman, far advanced in years, a Muslim, who believed in God and His Messenger in secret and outwardly went along with my family.
sentences.n: طَاعِنَةٌ فِي السِّنِّ, literally 'thrusting into age', is the idiom for being far on in years.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَبِي يَعْتَقِدُ فِيهَا بِمَا يَرَي عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْأَمَانَةِ وَالْعِفَّةِ وَكَانَ يُكْرِمُهَا وَيَزِيدُ فِي إِكْرَامِهَا وَكَانَ يَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّهَا فِي دِينِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna abī yaʿtaqidu fīhā bi-mā yarā ʿalayhā min al-amānati wa-al-ʿiffati wa-kāna yukrimuhā wa-yazīdu fī ikrāmihā wa-kāna yaʿtaqidu annahā fī dīnihi
sentences.l: And my father used-to-hold-belief in her by what he saw upon her of trustworthiness and chastity, and he used-to honour her and increase in honouring her, and he used-to believe that she was in his religion.
sentences.i: My father trusted her, for the honesty and chastity he saw in her, and he honoured her and honoured her ever more, believing that she shared his religion.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَبِرْتُ سَلَّمَنِي أَبِي إِلَيْهَا وَقَالَ خُذِيهِ رَبِّيهِ وَعَلِّمِيهِ أَحْوَالَ دِينِنَا وَأَحْسِنِي تَرْبِيَتَهُ وَقُومِي بِخِدْمَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kabirtu sallamanī abī ilayhā wa-qāla khudhīhi rabbīhi wa-ʿallimīhi aḥwāla dīninā wa-aḥsinī tarbiyatahu wa-qūmī bi-khidmatihi
sentences.l: So when I grew-big, my father handed me over to her and said, 'Take him, raise him, and teach him the conditions of our religion, and do-well his upbringing, and stand to his service.'
sentences.i: When I had grown, my father entrusted me to her and said, 'Take him, bring him up, teach him the ways of our religion, rear him well, and see to his needs.'

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْنِي الْعَجُوزُ وَعَلَّمَتْنِي دِينَ الْإِسْلَامِ مِنَ الْوُضُوءِ وَ فَرَائِضِ الْوُضُوءِ وَالصَّلَوٰةِ وَحَفَّظَتْنِي الْقُرْآنَ وَقَالَتْ لَا تَعْبُدِي سِوَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhatnī al-ʿajūzu wa-ʿallamatnī dīna al-islāmi min al-wuḍūʾi wa-farāʾiḍi al-wuḍūʾi wa-al-ṣalāwati wa-ḥaffaẓatnī al-qurʾāna wa-qālat lā taʿbudī siwā Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: So the old woman took me and taught me the religion of Islam: of the ablution, and the obligations of the ablution, and the prayer; and she made-me-memorise the Qurʾan, and she said, 'Do not worship other-than God, Most High.'
sentences.i: The old woman took me and taught me the religion of Islam, beginning with the ablution and its obligations, then the prayer; she had me learn the Qurʾan by heart and said, 'Worship none but God, the Most High.'
sentences.n: الْوُضُوءِ is written with the ablution's ordinary spelling, and الصَّلَوٰة takes the dagger alif over the و, the standard way of showing the long ā of this defective spelling. لَا تَعْبُدِي is the feminine form, though the old woman is addressing the boy; a slip kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَمَّمْتُ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ لِي يَا وَلَدِي اُكْتُمْ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ عَنْ أَبِيكَ وَلَا تُعْلِمْهُ بِهِ لِئَلَّا يَقْتُلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā tammamtu dhālika qālat lī yā waladī uktum hādhā al-amra ʿan abīka wa-lā tuʿlimhu bihi li-allā yaqtulaka
sentences.l: So when I completed that, she said to me, 'O my son, conceal this matter from your father, and do not let-him-know it, lest he kill you.'
sentences.i: When I had finished all that, she said to me, 'My son, keep this matter from your father, and do not tell him of it, or he will kill you.'

sentences.t: فَكَتَمْتُهُ عَنْهُ وَلَمْ أَزَلْ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ مُدَّةَ أَيَّامٍ قَلَائِلَ
sentences.tr: fa-katamtuhu ʿanhu wa-lam azal ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli muddata ayyāmin qalāʾila
sentences.l: So I concealed it from him, and I did not cease upon this state for a period of few days.
sentences.i: So I hid it from him, and remained in this state for some few days.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ مَاتَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَزَادَ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ فِي كُفْرِهِمْ وَ عُتُوِّهِمْ وَغُلُوِّهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qad mātati al-ʿajūzu wa-zāda ahlu al-madīnati fī kufrihim wa-ʿutuwwihim wa-ghuluwwihim
sentences.l: And the old woman had died, and the people of the city increased in their unbelief and their insolence and their excess.
sentences.i: Then the old woman died, and the people of the city grew still more unbelieving, insolent and extreme.
sentences.n: The three plural nouns end alike (-hum), giving a loose rhymed-prose cadence.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ عَلَى مَا هُمْ فِيهِ إِذْ سَمِعُوا مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum ʿalā mā hum fīhi idh samiʿū munādiyan yunādī
sentences.l: So while they were upon what they were in, when they heard a caller calling.
sentences.i: While they were in this condition, they heard a crier crying out.
sentences.n: The sentence is left hanging; the crier's words follow in the next sentence.

sentences.t: بِأَ عْلَى صَوْتِهِ مِثْلَ الرَّعْدِ الْقَاصِفِ سَمِعَهُ الْقَرِيبُ وَالْبَعِيدُ يَقُولُ يَا أَهْلَ هَٰذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ ارْجِعُوا عَنْ عِبَادَةِ النِّيرَانِ وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّٰهَ الْمَلِكَ الرَّحْمَٰنَ
sentences.tr: bi-aʿlā ṣawtihi mithla al-raʿdi al-qāṣifi samiʿahu al-qarību wa-al-baʿīdu yaqūlu yā ahla hādhihi al-madīnati irjiʿū ʿan ʿibādati al-nīrāni wa-aʿbudū allāha al-malika al-raḥmāna
sentences.l: At the highest of his voice, like the crashing thunder, the near-one and the far-one heard it, saying: 'O people of this city, turn back from the worship of the fires, and worship God, the King, the Merciful!'
sentences.i: At the top of his voice, loud as crashing thunder, so that far and near alike heard it, he cried: 'People of this city, turn back from the worship of fire, and worship God, the King, the Merciful!'
sentences.n: بِأَ عْلَى is printed as two words (با على); it is read as بِأَعْلَى 'at the highest (pitch) of', without changing a letter. The phrase completes the previous sentence: the crier cried at the top of his voice.

sentences.t: فَحَصَلَ عِنْدَ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَزَعٌ وَاجْتَمَعُوا عِنْدَ أَبِي وَهُوَ مَلِكُ الْمَدِينَةِ وَقَالُوا لَهُ مَا هَٰذَا الصَّوْتُ الْمُزْعِجُ الَّذِي سَمِعْنَاهُ فَدَهِشْنَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ فَزَعِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaṣala ʿinda ahli al-madīnati fazaʿun wa-ajtamaʿū ʿinda abī wa-huwa maliku al-madīnati wa-qālū lahu mā hādhā al-ṣawtu al-muzʿiju alladhī samiʿnāhu fa-dahishnā min shiddati fazaʿihi
sentences.l: So there occurred, among the people of the city, a terror; and they gathered at my father, and he was the king of the city, and they said to him: 'What is this disquieting voice that we heard? We were bewildered from the intensity of its terror.'
sentences.i: Terror seized the people of the city, and they gathered around my father, who was the king of the city, and said to him: 'What is this dreadful voice we have heard? We were bewildered by the violence of its terror.'
sentences.n: The youth's father is the king of the city. The final clause, فَدَهِشْنَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ فَزَعِهِ, runs on inside the crowd's speech; the pronoun in فَزَعِهِ refers back to الصَّوْت, the voice.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ لَا يَهُولَنَّكُمُ الصَّوْتُ وَلَا يُخَوِّفْكُمْ وَلَا يَرُدَّكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum lā yahūlannakumu al-ṣawtu wa-lā yukhawwifkum wa-lā yaruddakum ʿan dīnikum
sentences.l: So he said to them: 'Let not the voice alarm you, and let it not frighten you, and let it not turn you back from your religion.'
sentences.i: He said to them: 'Do not let the voice alarm you or frighten you, or turn you away from your religion.'
sentences.n: لَا + jussive (يُخَوِّفْكُمْ، يَرُدَّكُمْ) or + emphatic نَّ (يَهُولَنَّكُمُ) is the ordinary way of forbidding in the third person: 'let it not ...'.

sentences.t: فَمَالَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَى قَوْلِ أَبِي وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا مُكِبِّينَ عَلَى عِبَادَةِ النَّارِ وَزَادُوا فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ إِلَى مُدَّةِ سَنَةٍ لِمِيعَادِ مَا سَمِعُوا الصَّوْتَ الْأَوَّلَ
sentences.tr: fa-mālat qulūbuhum ilā qawli abī wa-lam yazālū mukibbīna ʿalā ʿibādati al-nāri wa-zādū fī ṭughyānihim ilā muddati sanatin li-mīʿādi mā samiʿū al-ṣawta al-awwala
sentences.l: So their hearts inclined to the saying of my father, and they did not cease bent-over upon the worship of the fire, and they increased in their rebellion up to the space of a year, to the appointed-time of what they heard the first voice.
sentences.i: Their hearts inclined to my father's word, and they did not cease to be devoted to the worship of fire, and grew still more rebellious, for the space of a year, until the anniversary of the day they first heard the voice.
sentences.n: لِمِيعَادِ مَا سَمِعُوا is compressed: 'to the appointed time of (the day) they heard'. The reading 'up to a year, matching the date of the first voice' fits what follows.

sentences.t: فَظَهَرَ لَهُمْ ثَانِيًا فَسَمِعُوهُ وَثَالِثًا عَلَى ثَلَٰثِ سِنِينَ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ مَرَّةً فَلَمْ يَزَالُوا عَاكِفِينَ عَلَى مَا هُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى نَزَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَقْتُ وَالسَّخَطُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ فَسُخِطُوا أَحْجَارًا سُودًا وَدَوَابَّهُمْ وَأَنْعَامَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ẓahara lahum thāniyan fa-samiʿūhu wa-thālithan ʿalā thalāthi sinīna fī kulli sanatin marratan fa-lam yazālū ʿākifīna ʿalā mā hum ʿalayhi ḥattā nazala ʿalayhimu al-maqtu wa-al-sakhaṭu min al-samāʾi baʿda ṭulūʿi al-fajri fa-sukhiṭū aḥjāran sūdan wa-dawābbahum wa-anʿāmahum
sentences.l: So it appeared to them a second time and they heard it, and a third, upon three years, in every year once; and they did not cease devoted upon that which they were upon, until there descended upon them the abhorrence and the wrath from the sky, after the rising of the dawn; and they were wrathed-into black stones, and their beasts and their cattle.
sentences.i: It sounded for them a second time, and they heard it, and a third time; once in every year for three years. Still they did not cease from their ways, until abhorrence and wrath came down upon them from heaven after the break of dawn, and they were struck with wrath and turned into black stones, they and their beasts and their cattle.
sentences.n: ثَلَٰثِ is printed ثلث, a defective spelling of ثَلَاثِ 'three', so it takes the dagger alif. فَسُخِطُوا أَحْجَارًا (literally 'they were wrathed stones') uses the passive of 'to be angry at' for 'to be changed by wrath into'; the sense is fixed by the story, which turned the city to stone.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَسْلَمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ هَٰذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ غَيْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-lam yaslam min ahli hādhihi al-madīnati ghayrī
sentences.l: And none was safe of the people of this city other-than-me.
sentences.i: None of the people of this city escaped but I.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ يَوْمِ جَرَتْ هَٰذِهِ الْحَرَكَةُ وَأَنَا عَلَى هَٰذِهِ الْحَالَةِ فِي صَلَٰوةٍ وَصِيَامٍ وَ تِلَاوَةِ قُرْآنٍ وَقَدْ عِيلَ صَبْرِي مِنَ الْوَحْدَةِ وَمَا عِنْدِي مَنْ يُؤْنِسُنِي
sentences.tr: wa-min yawmi jarat hādhihi al-ḥarakatu wa-anā ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati fī ṣalāwatin wa-ṣiyāmin wa-tilāwati qurʾānin wa-qad ʿīla ṣabrī min al-waḥdati wa-mā ʿindī man yuʾnisunī
sentences.l: And from the day this movement ran, and I am upon this state, in prayer and fasting and recitation of a Qurʾān; and my patience has been exhausted from the aloneness, and there is not with me one who keeps me company.
sentences.i: From the day this thing happened I have lived in this state, in prayer and fasting and recitation of the Qurʾān, and my patience has run out with the loneliness; I have no one to keep me company.
sentences.n: The final و of ـتِلَاوَةِ is printed at the end of one line with the rest of the word on the next; it is read as one word وَتِلَاوَةِ. صَلَٰوةٍ is printed صلوة, an old spelling of صَلَاة with و; the dagger alif shows how it is said. Note the youth says 'a Qurʾān' with tanwīn (قُرْآنٍ), as printed.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ قُلْتُ لَهُ وَقَدْ سُلِبَ لُبِّي يَا هَٰذَا الشَّابُّ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَرُوحَ مَعِي إِلَى مَدِينَةِ بَغْدَادَ وَتَنْظُرَ إِلَى الْعُلَمَاءِ وَالْفُقَهَاءِ وَتَزْدَادَ عِلْمًا وَفَهْمًا وَفِقْهًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qultu lahu wa-qad suliba lubbī yā hādhā al-shābbu hal laka an tarūḥa maʿī ilā madīnati baghdāda wa-tanẓura ilā al-ʿulamāʾi wa-al-fuqahāʾi wa-tazdāda ʿilman wa-fahman wa-fiqhan
sentences.l: So at that I said to him, and my mind had been plundered: 'O this youth, is there for you (a wish) that you go with me to the city of Baghdad, and look upon the learned-ones and the jurists, and increase in knowledge and understanding and jurisprudence?'
sentences.i: Then I said to him, my wits quite carried off: 'Young man, would you come with me to the city of Baghdad, and see the learned and the jurists, and grow in knowledge and understanding and law?'
sentences.n: يَا هَٰذَا الشَّابُّ 'O this youth' is a common Middle Arabic vocative, where Classical would say يَا أَيُّهَا الشَّابُّ; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ الَّتِي قُدَّامَكَ سَيِّدَةُ قَوْمِهَا وَحَاكِمَةٌ عَلَى رِجَالٍ وَخَدَمٍ وَغِلْمَانٍ وَعِنْدِي مَرْكَبٌ مَوْثُوقٌ بِالتُّجَّرِ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam anna al-jāriyata allatī quddāmaka sayyidatu qawmihā wa-ḥākimatun ʿalā rijālin wa-khadamin wa-ghilmānin wa-ʿindī markabun mawthūqun bi-al-tujjari
sentences.l: And know that the girl who is in front of you is the lady of her people, and a ruler over men and servants and lads; and with me is a ship made-fast with the merchants.
sentences.i: Know that the girl before you is the lady of her people, and a ruler over men and servants and boys; and I have a ship, well secured and manned with merchants.
sentences.n: مَوْثُوقٌ بِالتُّجَّرِ is obscure. مَوْثُوق means 'bound fast, secured' and التُّجَّر is read as 'the merchants' (plural of تَاجِر), but the printed letters could also point to 'merchandise' (a cargo-laden ship); the translation keeps the first reading and stays cautious.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَمَتْنَا الْمَقَادِيرُ عَلَى هَٰذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ حَتَّى كَانَ سَبَبًا فِي اطِّلَاعِنَا عَلَى هَٰذِهِ الْأُمُورِ وَكَانَ النَّصِيبُ فِي اجْتِمَاعِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad ramatnā al-maqādīru ʿalā hādhihi al-madīnati ḥattā kāna sababan fī iṭṭilāʿinā ʿalā hādhihi al-umūri wa-kāna al-naṣību fī ijtimāʿinā
sentences.l: And the decrees had cast us upon this city, so that it was a cause in our being-informed of these matters; and the lot was in our meeting.
sentences.i: The decrees of fate cast us upon this city, so that it became the cause of our learning of these things; and it was destiny that brought us together.
sentences.n: كَانَ سَبَبًا has a masculine verb though its subject, the casting, is only implied; read it as 'that (event) was a cause'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَزَلْ أُحَسِّنُ لَهُ التَّوَجُّهَ وَأُلَاطِفُهُ وَأَتَحَايَلُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى قَبِلَ وَأَنْعَمَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal uḥassinu lahu al-tawajjuha wa-ulāṭifuhu wa-ataḥāyalu ʿalayhi ḥattā qabila wa-anʿama bihi
sentences.l: And I did not cease making-fair to him the going, and being-gentle with him, and contriving upon him, until he accepted and said yes to it.
sentences.i: I kept making the journey seem good to him, coaxing him and using every device on him, until he accepted, and gladly agreed to it.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, so she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, breaking off the permitted talk.
sentences.n: The regular closing formula of each night; the rhyme -āḥ (ṣabāḥ / mubāḥ) is sajʿ.
